questions.question: A company wants developers to be able to create test environments in minutes instead of waiting weeks for hardware. Which cloud benefit does this describe?

options.why: Correct. Getting resources quickly so you can experiment and deliver faster is agility.
Predictability is about consistent performance and costs, not speed of provisioning.
Governance is about rules and compliance.
High availability is about keeping services running despite failures.

questions.explanation: Agility means you can provision and change resources quickly, which shortens time to market.

questions.question: Which TWO are common business reasons to adopt cloud computing?

options.why: Correct. Cloud shifts spending to pay-as-you-go.

options.text: Eliminating all security responsibilities for the customer
options.why: Customers always keep responsibilities such as data, identities and devices.
Correct. Scalability and elasticity are key cloud benefits.

options.text: Guaranteeing that costs will always be lower than on-premises
options.why: Costs depend on how you use the cloud. Lower cost is not guaranteed.

questions.explanation: Avoiding CapEx and scaling with demand are core benefits. Security is shared and savings depend on good management.

questions.question: Why can large cloud providers often offer lower unit prices than a company running its own datacenter?

options.why: Correct. Buying hardware, power and networking at huge volume lowers cost per unit.

options.text: They do not pay for electricity
options.why: Providers pay for power, though at large-volume rates.
Hardware fails everywhere. Providers design for failure.

questions.explanation: Economies of scale let providers operate more cheaply per unit and pass some of that saving to customers.

questions.scenario: A company moved 200 servers to Azure VMs without changing their size and leaves them all running 24/7. Its bill is higher than expected.
questions.question: What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Cloud is always more expensive than on-premises
options.why: Not true in general. It depends on how resources are used.

options.text: Resources were not right-sized or scaled to demand
options.why: Correct. Oversized, always-on VMs waste money. Right-size, autoscale and use reservations.

options.text: Azure charges for VMs only when they are stopped
options.why: Running (allocated) VMs incur compute charges. Deallocated VMs do not.

options.text: Azure does not support Windows Server

questions.explanation: Lift-and-shift without right-sizing or scaling is the most common cause of disappointing cloud bills.
